headline: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan assaulted and harassed in Italy by alleged Awami League supporters
summary: Azmeri Haque Badhan, in Venice for her film's premiere, was attacked with water and eggs. She alleges the assault was politically motivated due to her role in the student movement.
details: Noted actress Azmeri Haque Badhan reported being physically assaulted, pelted with water, soft drinks, and eggs in Italy. The incident occurred while she was with her brother and his family in Mestre, near Venice, where she is attending the 83rd Venice International Film Festival for her film “The Difficult Bride”. Her mobile phone was knocked from her hand and she was struck near her ear.

Badhan alleges the attackers targeted her for her active participation in the July-August 2024 student-led mass movement. She had publicly supported the movement and spoken to media outlets about the attacks on students. Some attackers reportedly identified themselves as members of the Awami League and Bangladesh Chhatra League, both of which have been banned.

During the harassment, Badhan stated she was forced to chant "Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu." The attackers attempted to record and livestream the incident for social media. Her brother's wife was also pushed, and a young child was present during the assault.

Following the incident, Badhan went live on Facebook, detailing the events and sharing videos. She described the attackers calling her a "July militant" and "July warrior." She asserted her participation in the movement and stated, "It will not be so easy to silence Azmeri Haque Badhan."

Badhan also mentioned that she learned Sajeeb Wazed Joy, son of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, was also in Venice and urged that the incident be brought to his attention. She condemned the attackers' "irrational behaviour" and their failure to move past such actions.

headline: 24 medical students injured as bus falls into ditch in Comilla
summary: Students from Sher-e-Bangla Medical College were traveling to Cox's Bazar for a study tour when the accident occurred in Daudkandi.
details: A bus carrying students from Sher-e-Bangla Medical College fell into a ditch in the Jinglatali area of Daudkandi, Comilla, on Tuesday morning around 4:30 AM.
According to Dr. Nayan De of the Daudkandi Upazila Health Complex, 24 students were injured in the crash, with nine of them in critical condition.
The critically injured students have been shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment.
The students were on a study tour heading toward Cox's Bazar when the vehicle veered off the road.
Highway police arrived quickly at the scene to rescue the passengers from the wreckage.
The driver and assistant of the bus fled the scene immediately after the accident, according to OC Prem Das of the Daudkandi Highway Police Station.
caption:
24 medical students injured in Comilla after their bus fell into a ditch during a study tour.

A bus carrying students from Sher-e-Bangla Medical College fell into a ditch in the Jinglatali area of Daudkandi, Comilla, on Tuesday morning around 4:30 AM.

According to Dr. Nayan De of the Daudkandi Upazila Health Complex, 24 students were injured in the crash, with nine of them in critical condition.

The critically injured students have been shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment.

The students were on a study tour heading toward Cox's Bazar when the vehicle veered off the road.

Highway police arrived quickly at the scene to rescue the passengers from the wreckage.

The driver and assistant of the bus fled the scene immediately after the accident, according to OC Prem Das of the Daudkandi Highway Police Station.
